inspection_summary: Inspected all 869 normalized lines of the article. The source develops structural restrictions on failures of Robin's inequality, asymptotic divisor/totient ratios on restricted integer classes, a canonical exponent-pattern reduction to Hardy-Ramanujan integers, and a minimal-counterexample plus analytic/computational proof for 5-free integers. Prose and most displayed mathematics are recoverable despite text-layer formula reordering; the display-dense proof of Lemma 14 at lines 709-728 is not safe enough to retain without scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: Title and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Front matter and source-level summary of the Robin criterion and the paper's structural counterexample restrictions.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines Robin's inequality, records the RH criterion and finite exceptions, and states the squarefree, odd, squarefull, 5-free, and fifth-power formulations.

sections_inspected.label: 2 Proof of Theorem 1 and Theorem 2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses reciprocal-prime bounds, induction, a largest-prime case split, totient strengthening, and squarefree-kernel invariance to prove the squarefree and odd cases.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1 Theorem 7 put into perspective
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies Nicolas's primorial behavior as an obstruction to extending the odd totient strengthening to even integers.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Proof of Theorem 4
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces squarefull exceptions to bounded prime support and a finite verified search using an explicit prime-product estimate.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Ratios on restricted integer sets
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Determines limsup constants for divisor-sum and totient ratios on unrestricted, squarefree, odd, squarefull, and t-free families.

sections_inspected.label: 5 Reduction to Hardy-Ramanujan integers
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Canonicalizes exponent patterns by assigning larger exponents to smaller primes and transfers Robin failures to the least representative.

sections_inspected.label: 6 Proof of Theorem 5 and method limit
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines minimal-counterexample descent, a largest-prime bound, Euler-product tail estimates, cascading cutoffs, and bounded computation to prove the 5-free result, then states the unresolved 6-free limitation of this method.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgement, references, and author data
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-mathematical back matter inspected for completeness and excluded from semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Robin inequality, RH criterion, and the finite exception baseline
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the central inequality and set R, records Robin's equivalence threshold and infinite-failure consequence, and identifies the checked exceptions below 5041 that anchor later reductions.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the definition, Robin result, and exception-set observation together because subsequent structural theorems depend on all three.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The divisor-sum display is slightly reordered by extraction, but the defining inequality and prose are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Squarefree and odd subfamilies reduce the RH check to even non-squarefree integers
accepted_units.why_material: Theorems 1 and 2 eliminate all but small exceptions in two broad families, and Theorem 3 converts them into a lower-density conditional test class for Robin's criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the density remark only as interpretation of the reduction, not as evidence toward RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted density formula is visually degraded; the theorem statements and decimal density are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Squarefull and 5-free exclusions yield a fifth-power formulation of Robin's criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Theorems 4 and 5 eliminate squarefull and 5-free candidates, while Theorem 6 packages the result as an RH-equivalent test on integers divisible by a prime fifth power and contrasts it with Lagarias's harmonic formulation.
accepted_units.context_note: The finite-exception observation at lines 87-95 is necessary for the equivalence, not merely motivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Superscripts and the harmonic-sum display should be checked against the retained PDF before exact formula reuse; the stated equivalences are readable.

accepted_units.title: Elementary reciprocal-prime estimate sufficient for the squarefree proof
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 1 supplies a deliberately elementary upper bound for the reciprocal-prime sum, with an explicit computation-to-asymptotic cutoff that later closes the small-largest-prime case.
accepted_units.context_note: The remarks distinguish the needed elementary strength from sharper but unnecessary prime-number estimates.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The sum and Mertens-constant displays have extraction reordering; exact constants and inequality orientation remain recoverable but merit PDF checking if quoted.

accepted_units.title: Adjoining a sufficiently large prime repairs the finite Robin exceptions
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 2 and its corollary turn finitely checked seed values into an infinite closure step by monotonicity in the adjoined prime, isolating three exceptional products at q=7.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the base-case repair mechanism used inside the squarefree induction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed ratio chain is readable from the surrounding prose and requires no external reconstruction.

accepted_units.title: Squarefree induction split by the largest prime relative to log n
accepted_units.why_material: The proof of Theorem 1 uses two complementary mechanisms: induction transfers Robin's inequality when the largest prime is large, while the reciprocal-prime bound controls the product when that prime is below log n.
accepted_units.context_note: The local inequalities and both cases must remain together; separating either case would hide why the split is exhaustive.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several multiline inequalities are reordered by extraction, but their transformations and the two-case logic are supported by adjacent prose.

accepted_units.title: Totient strengthening and squarefree-kernel invariance prove the odd case
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 7 replaces the divisor ratio by the stronger n/phi(n) bound, observes that this ratio depends only on the squarefree kernel, and compares an odd squarefree n to a smaller even squarefree n1 so Theorem 1 and a finite fallback apply.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 3 because it supplies the bounded-prime-support fallback when n1 is one of the squarefree exceptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Products and phi notation are partially reordered, but the comparison n/phi(n) < sigma(n1)/n1 and kernel argument are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Primorial totient behavior blocks extension of the odd-number strengthening
accepted_units.why_material: The source explicitly tests its proof route against even integers and uses the RH-dependent sign behavior of n/phi(n) on primorials to show that Theorem 7's stronger inequality cannot supply such an extension.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a source-identified failed generalization, not a proof failure of Robin's original inequality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The inequality and primorial definition are legible; no missing external context is needed for the stated obstruction.

accepted_units.title: Squarefull violations have bounded prime support and size
accepted_units.why_material: A Rosser-Schoenfeld product bound forces at most four distinct prime factors for a squarefull totient violation, which then bounds n and reduces Theorem 8 to finite verification; the a^2 b^3 representation supplies an enumeration method.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 8 is stronger than Theorem 4 and its finite exception list is part of the certification boundary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One product index in the extracted proof is garbled and the numerical bound should be scan-verified, but the bounded-support and finite-search mechanism is prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Limsup constants across unrestricted, squarefree, odd, and squarefull families
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 9 compares how structural restrictions change the maximal normalized divisor and totient ratios, and identifies Mertens's product asymptotic as the shared analytic input.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed eight-part theorem is retained as one comparison unit because its value is the cross-family pattern.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Columnar display order is degraded; exact pairing of parts and constants should be verified against the PDF before downstream serialization.

accepted_units.title: t-free limsup via large-prime suppression and a matching prime-power construction
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 6 proves the upper bound by separating primes above log n and truncating the Euler product, then proves sharpness on products of primes with exponent t-1 using Mertens and the prime number theorem; it also gives the odd analogue.
accepted_units.context_note: Upper and lower constructions are inseparable here because together they establish the exact limsup rather than a one-sided estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The long Euler-product displays are line-wrapped but recoverable; exact asymptotic factors should be checked against the PDF for formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Robin counterexamples would require unbounded prime exponents
accepted_units.why_material: Combining Robin's infinite-counterexample consequence under false RH with the fixed-t limsup bound shows that the maximum exponent along such counterexamples must tend to infinity.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a conditional structural consequence, not evidence that counterexamples exist.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The factorization display is reordered, but the max-exponent conclusion is explicit.

accepted_units.title: The ratio landscape follows by varying t and choosing squarefull extremizers
accepted_units.why_material: The proof of Theorem 9 derives unrestricted, squarefree, and odd constants as limits or special cases of Lemma 6, and realizes the squarefull lower bounds with uniform prime-power products.
accepted_units.context_note: The terse citations are not expanded; the unit records only the deductions present in the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The product notation at lines 550-555 is split by extraction but its role is clear from prose.

accepted_units.title: Testing Hardy-Ramanujan integers suffices up to any finite bound
accepted_units.why_material: Proposition 1 states a sparse canonical test set for Robin's inequality and quantifies its asymptotic count, setting up a representation-level reduction rather than a new criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof mechanism is supplied by the following exponent-pattern lemmas and is captured in separate units.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The defining prime-power product and asymptotic count are line-wrapped; exact typography needs PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Swapping exponents favors larger powers on smaller primes
accepted_units.why_material: Monotonicity of a rational function yields Lemma 8's exchange inequality, the local move that orders exponent assignments to maximize sigma(n)/n.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivative proof and the prime-exponent exchange are kept together to preserve why the rearrangement is valid.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The display at lines 598-612 is partially reordered, but the inequality direction and dependence on Lemma 7 are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Exponent patterns map every possible violation to a least canonical representative
accepted_units.why_material: The source defines exponent patterns and m(e-bar), proves that this smallest Hardy-Ramanujan representative maximizes sigma(n)/n within the pattern, and transfers any Robin failure to that representative.
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 10 supplies both contraposed directions needed to justify Proposition 1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Bars, products, and exponents are somewhat degraded, while the pattern definition, extremal property, and transfer claim remain readable.

accepted_units.title: A least t-free counterexample must have largest prime below log n
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 11 removes a largest prime factor, uses minimality and the finite exception structure to force the remainder into R, then shows q at least log n would preserve Robin's inequality by submultiplicativity.
accepted_units.context_note: The finite-exception branch and analytic branch are both required to establish the strict largest-prime cutoff.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integral comparison and ratio chain are readable despite line wrapping; exact formula transcription should use the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Bounded Hardy-Ramanujan verification for 5-free candidates
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 12 records the finite enumeration and verification counts for 5-free canonical integers with largest prime at most 73 and also gives an alternative route using a prior lower bound on counterexamples.
accepted_units.context_note: This is reported computational evidence from the source, not independently rerun verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The products in the alternative proof are reordered; the MAPLE counts and claimed coverage are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Euler-product tail estimates used to bound 5-free divisor ratios
accepted_units.why_material: Lemmas 13 and 14 state the explicit truncated-product and tail bounds that convert a largest-prime restriction into a numerical cutoff.
accepted_units.context_note: Only the recoverable lemma statements are selected; the extraction-defective proof display at lines 709-728 is excluded pending scan verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent unit: verify the exact logarithmic terms, product definitions, and constants against the retained PDF before use.

accepted_units.title: Tail control plus the explicit prime-product estimate proves the truncation bound
accepted_units.why_material: The source factors the truncated t-free Euler product into the zeta value and tail, applies Lemma 14, and combines the result with Lemma 4 to obtain Lemma 13.
accepted_units.context_note: This captures the readable composition step without reconstructing the defective intermediate proof of Lemma 14.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The first product identity is line-wrapped but recoverable; exact display form should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Cascading numerical bounds reduce a 5-free counterexample to largest prime at most 73
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 15 repeatedly feeds an upper bound for the truncated Euler product back into a bound on log m, shrinking the admissible prime cutoff from 193 through a finite cascade to 73.
accepted_units.context_note: The stopping point is justified in-source by failure of the next numerical reduction, so the cascade has a defined endpoint.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This unit depends on extracted numerical formulae; verify P5 values and exponential constants against the PDF before exact computational reuse.

accepted_units.title: Minimality, canonicalization, and finite verification prove all 5-free integers satisfy Robin
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 5 assembles Lemmas 11, 15, 10, and 12: a least counterexample has small largest prime, must equal its canonical exponent-pattern representative except for a separately bounded case, and both routes contradict its failure.
accepted_units.context_note: The final small-pattern branch is retained because it closes a gap not covered directly by the canonical representative argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The five-prime factorization and product bound are extraction-degraded; the branch structure and final MAPLE contradiction are explicit.

accepted_units.title: The proof method does not presently extend from 5-free to 6-free integers
accepted_units.why_material: The authors identify substantial computational cost as the barrier to the immediate extension and point to a different, less self-contained proposed approach as future work.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an explicit source-level limitation, not a claim that a 6-free theorem is false.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Pure prose; no representation dependency.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Structural funnel for any large Robin counterexample
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Within the source's proved reductions, a counterexample beyond the finite baseline is forced away from squarefree, odd, squarefull, and 5-free classes, hence must be even, non-squarefree, non-squarefull, and divisible by a prime fifth power.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is conditional filtering under Robin's criterion and source-reported finite computations; it neither produces a counterexample nor proves RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Canonical exponent-pattern compression of divisor-ratio searches
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For each exponent multiset, exchange monotonicity places larger exponents on smaller primes, producing the least integer and largest divisor ratio in the pattern, so a Robin search can be compressed to Hardy-Ramanujan representatives.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The transfer is patternwise and depends jointly on monotonicity of sigma(n)/n and the smaller logarithmic threshold; it is not an unrestricted monotonicity claim.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Largest-prime cutoff pipeline for the 5-free theorem
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Minimality first forces P(n)<log n; explicit Euler-product bounds then cascade to P(n)<=73; exponent-pattern canonicalization finally connects the candidate to a finite verified family.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact numerical constants and MAPLE enumeration are source-reported, and formula-sensitive steps require PDF or computational verification before reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Restricted-family asymptotics explain both exclusions and residual risk
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Fixed exponent caps lower the attainable normalized divisor ratio, while matching prime-power constructions attain the bounds; consequently any infinite Robin-failure sequence would need unbounded exponents.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The unbounded-exponent conclusion is conditional on the source's stated false-RH consequence and does not identify the scale or form of such integers.
